title: Stacked words
prompt:
In this kind of puzzle the layout is part of the clue. Read the words together with the way they are placed.

```
HEAD
HEELS
```

The stack stands for a common three-word phrase about being completely in love. What is the phrase?
hints: What does the position of the first word, compared with the second, tell you?
Which small linking word describes one thing being placed above another?
If you read the first word, then that linking word, then the second word aloud, do you get a phrase you have heard before?
solution:
**Head over heels.**

HEAD sits above HEELS, so the missing word is a word for "above": OVER. Reading the layout aloud gives *head over heels*, the phrase for being madly in love.

In a rebus puzzle the position of the words carries part of the message, so ask what the arrangement is saying as well as what the words say.
